html:
A huge public works programme that remade Paris between 1853 and 1870, ordered by Emperor Napoleon III and run by his prefect, Georges Eugène Haussmann.

Old Paris was crowded, dark and dirty, with narrow medieval lanes, and cholera had struck it more than once. Haussmann cut long straight boulevards through it, tearing down whole quarters. Along them rose the uniform cream stone apartment blocks that still define the city. Engineers built new sewers and aqueducts for clean water, and parks such as the Bois de Boulogne and the Buttes Chaumont. New railway stations, markets and the Opera followed.

The work had critics. It cost a fortune, drove the poor out to the edges, and the wide streets were also easier for troops to clear of barricades, a lesson of the 1848 revolution. Haussmann was dismissed in 1870, just before the empire fell. His Paris became the model of a modern capital, copied in cities from Brussels to Buenos Aires.
sum: A huge public works programme that remade Paris between 1853 and 1870, ordered by Emperor Napoleon III and run by his prefect, Georges Eugène Haussmann.
